pages.text: Your class sets your combat role: it changes your HP and weapon effectiveness, and gives you passive abilities and one active skill. Classes are an $(bold)Origins$() layer, separate from your Race.$(br2)There are $(bold)13 classes$(), all viable; none is the 'best', each suits a different playstyle. Ten have a page here (the Elemental, Blessed and Corrupted do not yet).

$(bold)Respeccing Your Class$()$(br2)You change class at a $(bold)Class Altar$(), a station you craft. A respec there costs a tier-appropriate boss drop and 30 XP levels, and you keep your skill points. Players on a server can share one altar.$(br2)$(bold)Races are permanent.$() You choose your race when you create your character, and it can never be changed.

$(bold)Three Layers of Identity$()$(br2)$(bold)Race$(): what you are. Innate traits with mild tradeoffs. Permanent.$(br)$(bold)Class$(): what you do. Combat role, HP modifier, weapon affinities and an active ability. You can respec it.$(br)$(bold)Skills$(): how you invest. Bonuses that add up across six trees. A respec costs 5 levels per point.

The three layers stack additively. An $(thing)Orc$() $(thing)Berserker$() with points in the Warfare tree is a very different character from an $(thing)Elf$() Berserker.$(br2)$(bold)Next: undecided? $(l:icraft:welcome/class_guide)Origin, Race & Class$(/l) matches classes to playstyles.$()

$(bold)Half Equipment HP Rule$()$(br2)$(thing)Ranger$(), $(thing)Archmage$() and $(thing)Void Summoner$() get only 50% of every max HP bonus from equipment, including the Vitality enchant, HP affixes and armor attribute modifiers.$(br2)It $(italic)does not affect$() base HP, Spice of Life food HP or JustLevelingFork level-up HP. These glass cannons have a lower HP ceiling, but food diversity and leveling still pay off for them.
